clue.text: Clip of Hitchcock pitching for location of pilot

indicators.note: a clip is a short excerpt cut from a longer film, so the answer is a stretch snipped out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the director's name into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A film clip of Alfred Hitchcock throwing a baseball, or pitching an idea to a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' fits the film-director surface so neatly that it reads as movie footage; here it is the instruction to cut a run of letters out of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockpit is the compartment where an aircraft's pilot sits, so 'location of pilot' is a plain descriptive definition.

clue.text: Police eastern woodland

parts.note: cops is the everyday word for police officers
E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern

explanation.surface: An instruction to police officers to patrol a stretch of eastern woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like a verb in the surface; it is the noun, and the plural slang for officers supplies the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood of trees or undergrowth, so 'woodland' is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Repair scratched keel and prepare for action

indicators.note: to repair something is to rebuild it from its parts, so the letters that follow are put back together in a new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boatyard job: mend a keel that has been scraped, and get the vessel ready to sail again.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical surface hides the fact that the answer is nautical too; 'Repair' sounds like shipwright's work but is only telling you to rebuild the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: On a warship the decks were cleared of loose gear before battle, and the phrase now means getting ready for any big undertaking.

clue.text: Stiff old part for piano

parts.note: someone prim is stiffly formal and proper
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A stuffy old piece of music written for the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff old' reads as a description of the piano part; split it, and each word is a separate piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the primo is the upper part, played by the pianist on the right, as against the secondo below.

clue.text: Handle land-worker

definitions.meaning: a noun here: the lever a helmsman pushes to turn a small boat's rudder
one who works the soil by ploughing and turning it

explanation.surface: A job title: the person who handles the work on the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb governing 'land-worker'; it is a noun, and the same word names both a boat part and a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is both the lever that steers a small boat and, literally, someone who tills the ground.

clue.text: A party in outskirts of Sevenoaks returned drinks

indicators.note: returned means the whole assembled string is sent back, read right to left
'in' places the party between the outskirts
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Sevenoaks, a town in Kent
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Guests at a party on the edge of a Kent town came back for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives SS from Sevenoaks (a town in Kent), A and DO go 'in' to make SADOS, and 'returned' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodas are fizzy soft drinks, so the word is a plural example of drinks.

clue.text: Do well and draw in one of the best players, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.words: draw in one of the best players
parts.note: to suck is to draw in, and a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A tennis draw: a player does well and lands one of the top seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' pulls you toward the tournament draw the surface describes, but 'draw in' is breathing or sipping. Seeds are the players ranked highest so they avoid each other early.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to achieve what you set out to, so 'Do well' is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Carelessly I never rinsed last piece of plastic tableware

indicators.note: done carelessly, a thing comes out in no particular order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the phrase to be scrambled

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word, added to the mix

explanation.surface: A confession of sloppy washing-up: someone never rinsed the last plastic plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last piece of plastic' reads like an item of crockery; it is just the final letter, the C that joins the twelve scrambled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a matching set of plates and dishes for a meal, a particular kind of tableware.

clue.text: Mollify supporter crushed by recent information from the south

indicators.note: something crushed by a thing is squeezed inside it, so the first piece goes within the second
in a down clue, read from the south means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: news is recent information
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Soothing a fan who has been flattened by the latest reports coming up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan crushed by bad news; it is the peg that holds up a golf ball. The reversal applies after the insertion, so the finished word is read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten someone is to soften them up or make them more agreeable, which is what mollifying does.

clue.text: Translation of one Celtic epic shows creative expression

indicators.note: a translation renders the same material in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary note: a translator's version of an old Celtic epic takes creative liberties.
explanation.walkthrough: Translators really do take liberties with epics, which is why the surface feels true; the translation here is of letters, not of language.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom a writer takes to bend fact or grammar for effect, a kind of creative expression.

clue.text: Nobleman with medal in place of jewellery?

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, awarded as a medal

explanation.surface: A decorated aristocrat standing in a jeweller's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places a nobleman with his medal in a jewellery shop; the place is on the head, and the question mark flags that the definition is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is where earrings are worn, so it is a place for jewellery, defined by what hangs from it.

clue.text: Key opening part of Olympic Games?

parts.note: E is one of the musical keys
a vent is an opening that lets air or smoke out

explanation.surface: Asking which ceremony forms the key opening part of the Olympic Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key opening' reads as the grand opening ceremony. Split it: a musical key gives one letter, and 'opening' is a noun for a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympics are made up of individual events, the 100 metres or the high jump, so an event is one part of the Games.

clue.text: Primarily sandy, arid, hot and rainless area

definitions.text: Primarily sandy, arid, hot and rainless area
definitions.note: An &lit: the whole clue describes the answer, while the same words supply its letters through their initials.

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so it asks for the first letters of the words that follow

parts.words: sandy, arid, hot and rainless area
parts.note: the first letter of each of the six words, in order

explanation.surface: A geography-textbook description of a scorching, rainless desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word earns twice: read straight it describes one famous desert, and its initials spell that desert's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the vast North African desert, as sandy, arid, hot and dry as the clue says.

clue.text: Consequently allowed petition

parts.note: so means therefore, consequently
licit means permitted, the opposite of illicit

explanation.surface: A court's verdict that a petition was, in the end, allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a legal ruling on a petition; 'petition' is really a verb, and 'Consequently allowed' is two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for something earnestly, which is what petitioning someone means.

clue.text: Eggs reportedly expensive for some inhabitants of the countryside

parts.note: roe is a mass of fish eggs

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: something expensive is dear

explanation.surface: A grumble that eggs are said to be pricey for country dwellers.
explanation.walkthrough: The price-of-eggs surface points at rural shoppers; the eggs are fish eggs, and 'dear' only has to sound right.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are small deer that live wild across European woods and fields, so they are some of the countryside's inhabitants.

clue.text: Scientist backing team working

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word before it is read in reverse

parts.note: a side is a team
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A scientist throwing his support behind a working team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support; it is the instruction to turn the team round.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb, is a scientist by the looser crossword sense of the word.

clue.text: Supply safest meals

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, supply means bendily, so the letters that follow are bent into a new shape

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to cater the safest possible meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb but the adverb from 'supple', pronounced SUP-lee; in a supple manner, the letters flex.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts are large, lavish meals, so 'meals' covers them as a broader plural.

clue.text: Boy starts to look everywhere for implement

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A boy starting to hunt all over the kitchen for a utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to look' reads as the boy beginning his search; 'starts' is a noun here, the initials of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep long-handled spoon for serving soup, a kitchen implement.

clue.text: Sanction me going back alongside British ship

indicators.note: going back means travelling in reverse, so the word before it is read backwards

parts.note: the word is used as it stands
B is the standard abbreviation for British
the Argo was Jason's ship in the Greek myth of the Golden Fleece

explanation.surface: Someone asking permission to sail back beside a British vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' can mean approval or its opposite, a penalty; here it is the penalty. The Argo is crosswords' favourite ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade with a country, one of the commonest forms of international sanction.

clue.text: Prohibits importing European foodstuff

indicators.note: a thing importing something brings it inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: to prohibit something is to ban it
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A government blocking imports of a European food product.
explanation.walkthrough: The trade-policy surface makes 'importing' sound literal; it just means holding a letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are a staple food, so 'foodstuff' is a broad category that includes them.

clue.text: Top dirty — covered with grease?

indicators.note: to top something is to cut its head off, so the first letter of the next word goes

parts.note: soiled means dirty
the head letter removed

explanation.surface: A grubby, greasy top, like a mechanic's shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment in the surface; it is the verb meaning behead, which in a down clue lops off the letter at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oiled has had oil or grease applied to it; the question mark allows the loose match of grease for oil.

clue.text: Dog destroyed coke in parcels

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters that follow are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sniffer dog at customs wrecking packages to reach cocaine hidden inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug-bust surface suggests a sniffer dog tearing open packages; the thing destroyed is the letters, 'in' included.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocker spaniel is a breed of small gundog with long silky ears, so 'Dog' is a definition by category.

clue.text: Weapon is part of Beretta series

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the words that follow, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the gun maker's name into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A catalogue note that a gun belongs to one of Beretta's model lines.
explanation.walkthrough: BERETTA is an Italian firearms maker, which makes the surface's weapon look like a pistol; the one in the answer is electric.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun that fires wired darts to deliver an electric shock, so it is a weapon.

clue.text: Hold up South American writer before introduction to DC

indicators.note: the introduction to something is its opening, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south
US stands for the United States, so for American
a pen is the thing that writes
the first letter of DC

explanation.surface: A South American author delaying a trip until after arriving in Washington, DC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American writer' reads as one novelist from that continent; split it, three words give three pieces, and the writer is a pen, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something up is to delay or halt it, and to suspend is to put it on hold, so the two mean the same.
